title: stormcell throughput sketch
body:
Quick context:
- Personal scratchpad for a throughput / microburst run I started after noticing weird p99 spikes during short-lived surges on the staging fleet. Goal: reproduce, isolate whether KV cache priming or batch formation is the main culprit, and sketch mitigations.

Hypothesis to test:
1) Short bursts (200-800ms windows) are suffering from ineffective prefix caching: first-in-burst requests flow to cold lanes and trigger longer model decode overheads.
2) Batching threshold timer + low arrival variance exacerbates p95->p99 spread.
3) Small changes to max_batch_delay and early-compact scheduling can reduce p99 with minimal p50 impact.

Environment / harness:
- Model: llamax-13b-quant (8-bit), KV cache enabled
- Fleet: single A100 pod on staging, kernel build 2025-09-18
- Runner: bench-runner v0.34 (local harness reproducer)
- Load generator: custom python harness (attached in PR link), poisson arrival with imposed microburst overlay
- Payload: chat-like prompts, seq_len distribution: 80% <= 64 tokens, 15% 65-256, 5% >256 (to capture varied decode lengths)
- Metrics captured: p50/p90/p95/p99 latency, decode tokens/sec, batch size distribution, kv-cache-hit, concurrency, GPU util

Commands used (notes):
- baseline: bench-runner --qps 120 --burst-profile short-bursts.json --max-batch-delay-ms 6 --duration 10m
- tuned: bench-runner --qps 120 --burst-profile short-bursts.json --max-batch-delay-ms 3 --early-compact --duration 10m
- warm priming: prefill script to push 20 low-cost requests to populate prefix KV between bursts

Observations (first pass):
- Baseline run (max_batch_delay=6ms): p50 ~ 38ms, p95 ~ 220ms, p99 ~ 620ms. Batch sizes: median 4, tail batches hitting 1-2 frequently during burst onset. KV cache hit ~ 0.28 at burst start, rises to 0.76 mid-burst.
- Tuned run (max_batch_delay=3ms + early-compact): p50 ~ 40ms (slight increase), p95 ~ 180ms, p99 ~ 310ms. Tail batches reduced; more consistent batch sizes of 3-5. KV cache hit increased earlier (0.5 at burst onset).
- Warm priming only: p99 dropped to ~420ms but p95 unchanged; suggests priming alone helps cold-keycases but scheduling needed for top improvement.

Quick diagnostics:
- Trace sample: 2025-11-03T14:12:03Z - cold request path shows 120ms extra on model-init path where KV deserialization occurs (~30ms) + kernel schedule jitter (~80ms).
- GPU util: spikes to 95% on decode peaks, but most of tail still in CPU scheduling/queueing.
- Observed a recurring pattern where a small number of requests with long sequences (>256 tokens) arriving as first-in-burst cause large decode time for subsequent requests (head-of-line effect).

Preliminary conclusions:
- Reducing max_batch_delay and enabling early-compact reduces p99 most effectively for these short bursts. This trades off small p50 regression likely due to increased scheduling overhead.
- KV cache priming helps but is insufficient on its own; need combined approach (priming + faster scheduling).
- Consider head-of-line mitigation: detect long-seq first-request and route to dedicated lane or preemptive small-batch path.

Next experiments (short list):
- Run same harness on H100 node to rule out kernel scheduling differences (A100 vs H100).
- Add experiment with sequence-length aware batching that separates >256 tokens into a slow lane. Compare to baseline.
- Test adaptive batching: dynamically lower max_batch_delay at burst onset for first 200ms. Measure p99 improvement and p50 impact.
- Measure effect of increasing KV cache TTL / retention to boost hit rate between microbursts.

Notes / TODOs:
- Share raw traces and flame graphs with Ethan; ask SRE to correlate pod-level CPU scheduling during the 14:12 trace.
- Follow-up: draft small PR to add early-compact flag to canary image and run distributed experiment across 3 pods.
- If adaptive batching shows >30% p99 improvement with <10% p50 regression, propose default change for staging tuning.

Random ideas recorded (brain dump):
- Could we pre-classify incoming requests by a cheap token-length estimator at edge proxy to steer scheduling?
- Backpressure knob per-tenant: temporarily decrease max inflight for noisy tenants during detected microbursts.

Attachments / artifacts referenced: bench harness (GH PR), replay traces (confluence link), jira ticket ENG-1297 for epic tracking.

End of sketch. Keep this as my working log — will convert to proper runbook if experiments replicate across hardware.
